catwalk.definition: Narrow platform extending out into an auditorium.

backstage.definition: A stage area out of sight of the audience.

front-row.definition: Seats nearest the stage, podium, or front of a room form the front row.

lighting-rig.definition: A supporting structure that holds stage or event lights and related equipment.
lighting-rig.exampleUsage: The lighting rig was installed above the runway.

sound-system.definition: A group of electronic devices plays recorded sound or increases its volume throughout a particular room, hall, or vehicle.

backdrop.definition: A background placed behind a subject or scene.

stage.definition: A specific identifiable position in a continuum or series or especially in a process.

seating.definition: An area that includes places where several people can sit.

press-area.definition: A designated section where journalists, photographers, and other media workers can report on an event.
press-area.exampleUsage: Photographers gathered in the press area.

vip-section.definition: A reserved area for specially invited or high-profile guests.
vip-section.exampleUsage: The VIP section was separated from the general seating.

casting.definition: The act of creating something by casting it in a mold.

fitting.definition: A small and often standardized accessory to a larger system.

rehearsal.definition: A practice session in preparation for a public performance (as of a play or speech or concert).

hair-styling.definition: Arranging a person’s hair to create a selected shape or appearance.

makeup.definition: An event that is substituted for a previously cancelled event.

lineup.definition: The schedule of programs for a particular period.

choreography.definition: The representation of dancing by symbols as music is represented by notes.

music-selection.definition: A group of musical pieces chosen to suit a particular event, activity, or performance.

invitations.definition: A request (spoken or written) to participate or be present or take part in something.

fashion-week.definition: A series of fashion-industry events in which designers and brands present new collections.
fashion-week.exampleUsage: Several designers presented collections during fashion week.

paris.definition: The capital and largest city of France.

milan.definition: The capital of Lombardy in northern Italy.

new-york.definition: A major city in the United States known for business, culture, media, and fashion.
new-york.exampleUsage: New York hosts major fashion events each year.

london.definition: The capital and largest city of England.

designer.definition: A person who devises plots or intrigues.

label.definition: Trade name of a company that produces musical recordings.

maison.definition: Une maison désigne un foyer comme lieu de vie, groupe social et symbole, avec ses habitants et son organisation familiale.

fashion-editor.definition: An editor who selects, reviews, or manages fashion content for a publication or media outlet.
fashion-editor.exampleUsage: The fashion editor took notes during the runway show.

photographer.definition: A person who takes photographs, especially for newspapers and news reports.

fashion-blog.definition: A website or online publication focused mainly on clothing, style, designers, and fashion news.
fashion-blog.exampleUsage: The fashion blog published a review of the collection.

magazine.definition: A thin publication with articles and pictures, released regularly.

review.definition: An article that evaluates a book, film, product, or event.

coverage.definition: The extent to which something is covered.

social-media.definition: Websites and apps that let users create, share, and interact with content and other people online.
social-media.exampleUsage: The event posted official photos on social media.

influencer.definition: A person who has a large following on one or more social media platform that works to generate interest in contemporary social issues and/or advertise consumer products.

street-style.definition: Fashion based on clothing worn by people in everyday public settings rather than only on formal runways.
street-style.exampleUsage: The photographer documented street style outside the venue.

red-carpet.definition: A strip of red carpeting laid out for dignitaries or other honored guests to walk along.
